screens.prompt: Put the typical reading into C2, choosing the summary that one noisy reading cannot drag.

hints.func-median: A mean moves when one reading moves; the middle of the list does not, and that is a different function.
hints.require-ref: Read the readings from B2:B6 instead of listing them in the formula.
hints.value: Sorted, the five readings are 12, 14, 15, 18, 19: the middle one is 15.
hints.error: #NUM! means the range held no numbers, so there was no middle to take. Check that it covers column B and not the reading labels in column A.

reject.why: the mean, 15.6, which is a different summary and is dragged by outliers
the middle of three readings, 14, which ignores half the data
the middle of four readings, 16, which is an average of two of them
the first reading is outside the range, so the reported middle is not the list's
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs

screens.prompt: The audit has an even number of readings, so put the median into C2 and accept the half-way value.

hints.syntax: The range grew by one row, so the reference has to grow with it: =MEDIAN(B2:B7).
hints.func-median: An even count has no single middle element, and MEDIAN handles that for you.
hints.require-ref: Read all six readings from the sheet so a new one is picked up automatically.
hints.value: The middle two are 15 and 18, so the median is the half-way value, 16.5.
hints.error: A word typed inside the brackets gives #VALUE!. Readings left blank in the grid are skipped quietly.

reject.why: the mean, 19.67, pulled up by the last reading
the odd-count median, 15, which ignores the newest reading
the range starts one row late, so the oldest reading is dropped
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
the median of the first four readings, 16, taken before the outlier arrived

docs.explain:
MEDIAN returns the middle value once the numbers are put in order. Half the readings sit above it and half below, so one extreme figure barely moves it. With an odd count the answer is one of the values on the sheet.

The first screen has five readings, 12, 18, 14, 19 and 15, which sort to 12, 14, 15, 18 and 19, so the answer is 15. The second screen adds a reading of 40, and the mean over the six climbs to 19.67. MEDIAN returns 16.5 instead, the half-way point between 15 and 18.

Blanks and text are ignored rather than counted as zero, so MEDIAN copes with a column that is still being filled. Point at the range and not at the six figures, or the next reading gets left out.

errors.text: The range holds no numbers at all, so there is no middle value to report.
A word was passed as an argument, as in =MEDIAN("n/a"), so it cannot join the sort.
A range that stops one row short changes the answer: five readings give 15 where six give 16.5.

docs.atWork: An audit report where one late-night reading should not move the typical figure, and salary bands quoted as medians.
docs.outcome: Summarise a list with a middle value that an outlier cannot drag.
docs.teaches: MEDIAN, and why it differs from AVERAGE
docs.dataset: Five and six audit readings with one outlier

seo.title: MEDIAN in Excel: the middle value
seo.description: AVERAGE moves with one wild reading; MEDIAN does not, because it returns the middle value. With an even count you get the half-way number, like 16.5.
